purpose: Targeted repairs to reviewed reconstruction sheets; composite only the specified repaired quadrants after visual validation and preserve all other source pixels.

input.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Input image 1 is the current four-panel reconstruction sheet of an already approved picnic table. Correct ONLY the BOTTOM-RIGHT overhead panel. Keep the other three panels, their framing, structure, colours, weathering, pixels and positions unchanged. The top-left front and top-right rear clearly show FIVE tabletop planks. The current overhead mistakenly shows FOUR. Replace only that tabletop in the bottom-right panel with exactly FIVE parallel full-length timber planks, separated by exactly FOUR narrow longitudinal gaps, maintaining the same overall tabletop outline and total width. Each plank occupies one fifth of the tabletop width; keep the existing two attached benches, supports, table length, their positions, all outer margins and overhead orientation unchanged. This is a true vertical overhead image of the SAME five-plank table shown above, not a redesigned table. Keep existing wood type, silvery weathering, grain scale, restrained colour and neutral studio lighting. Do not count the two separate benches as tabletop planks. Do not add a sixth plank, paint decorative stripes, alter the three approved panels, add labels or change the precise equal 2 by 2 panel grid. Output the entire square four-panel sheet at the same resolution. The repaired overhead must visibly have five actual solid planks and four continuous seams from one table end to the other.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Input image 1 is the current four-panel sheet of an already approved steel fire ring. TOP-LEFT FRONT is authoritative for the design and must remain unchanged. Correct TOP-RIGHT REAR, BOTTOM-LEFT SIDE and BOTTOM-RIGHT OVERHEAD only. Preserve the same ring diameter, low shell height, grate size and offset, rust finish, ash, two uprights and single coiled handle. STRUCTURAL INVARIANT: BOTH upright supports are mounted on the INSIDE face of the shell, as shown in top-left; there are NO exterior support straps, no exterior vertical brackets and no new exterior bolt heads. REAR REPAIR: look from behind the support side, with the handle on image-left; the near ring wall must naturally OCCLUDE the lower parts of both inside uprights. Only the portions above the near rim and their actual interior-facing surfaces may remain visible. Keep the grate projecting from that near support side inward toward the far chamber. SIDE REPAIR: retain the camera looking along the support axis but put the near upright behind the shell, hiding its lower section behind the near wall; eliminate the invented outside strap and bolts without moving the support or handle. OVERHEAD REPAIR: true exact vertical nadir, not an elevated oblique view. The round shell must project as a CIRCLE, with only its top rim and interior visible and no exterior sidewall band. Keep support side at image-TOP, open chamber at image-BOTTOM, and the single coiled handle on image-RIGHT, matching the authoritative front handedness. Both upright tops sit just INSIDE the rim. Grate extends inward from the top-side support axis toward the centre; preserve the same bar count and spacing. Do not mirror the hardware, move the supports to the outside, change the grate footprint, add a handle or duplicate parts. Keep all objects complete within their respective equal quadrants and preserve plain studio background, lighting and exact 2 by 2 panel layout with no text, borders or captions. Output the entire square sheet at the same resolution.
